metadata.topic: Solubility — Reading Solubility from Graph and Calculating Mass Precipitated on Cooling
metadata.note: Q1eii(1m): read solubility at 65°C from graph → ~100g per 100cm³. Q1f(2m): calculate mass precipitated when 100g/100cm³ solution cooled to 35°C where solubility≈48g/100cm³. Mass precipitated = 100 - 48 = 52g ±5%. Combined into one file. Own-figure tolerance wide for graph-dependent Q1eii.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q1e(ii) and Q1f — Solubility Graph: Read and Calculate Mass Precipitated
question.text:
A solubility curve shows how the solubility of a salt changes with temperature.

(e)(ii) Use the graph to determine the solubility of the salt at 65 °C. (1 mark)

Solubility at 65 °C = [[1]] g per 100 cm³

(f) A saturated solution of the salt is prepared at 65 °C using 100 cm³ of water. The solution is then cooled to 35 °C.

Calculate the mass of salt that precipitates when the solution is cooled from 65 °C to 35 °C. (2 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Reading solubility from the curve:

At 65 °C: solubility ≈ 100 g per 100 cm³

At 35 °C: solubility ≈ 48 g per 100 cm³

Calculating mass precipitated:

Mass precipitated = solubility at 65°C − solubility at 35°C

= 100 − 48 = 52 g

Why? At 65°C, 100g of salt dissolved in 100cm³ water (saturated). At 35°C, only 48g can remain dissolved → the excess (52g) crystallises out as precipitate.

steps.label:
Solubility from graph: read g per 100 cm³ at each temperature
At 65°C: ~100 g/100 cm³ | At 35°C: ~48 g/100 cm³
Read solubility at 65 °C from the graph. (1 mark)
Calculate mass of salt that precipitates on cooling to 35 °C. (2 marks)

fields.label: Solubility at 65 °C = _____ g per 100 cm³
fields.diagnostic_hint: Read the solubility curve at temperature 65°C. The value should be approximately 100 g per 100 cm³ (accept 90–110 based on graph reading tolerance).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: To read from a solubility curve: find 65°C on the x-axis, draw a vertical line up to the curve, then read horizontally across to the y-axis to get the solubility value in g per 100 cm³.

fields.label: Solubility at 35 °C = _____ g per 100 cm³
fields.diagnostic_hint: Read the solubility at 35°C from the graph — approximately 48 g per 100 cm³.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Read the solubility at 35°C from the curve: approximately 48 g per 100 cm³.

fields.label: Mass of salt precipitated = _____ g
fields.diagnostic_hint: Mass precipitated = solubility at 65°C − solubility at 35°C = 100 − 48 = 52 g. Accept own-figure: (your 65°C value) − (your 35°C value).

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Mass precipitated = solubility at start temperature − solubility at end temperature = 100 − 48 = 52 g. The excess that was dissolved at 65°C but can no longer stay in solution at 35°C crystallises out.
